doc.title: Lonnie Liston Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 9, 2021

title: Opening, 80th birthday and warming up at the piano
summary: Rowe opens the interview; Smith, just turned 80, describes his playing routine and how creative sparks come, including at Manny's keyboard store.

story.theme_name: Opening the interview: Monk Rowe's welcome and archive boilerplate
story.community_name: Opening the Hamilton College interview: introductions and boilerplate

blocks.x: My name is Monk Rowe and I’m very privileged to have Lonnie Liston Smith with me today for the Fillius Jazz Archive oral history program. Thanks for joining me.
You look well, am I correct that you just celebrated your 80th birthday not long ago?
Oh yeah, yeah, the 28th of December.
So you’re in your home, you’re sitting in front of your piano. When you go to your instrument these days just to play, do you have any kind of routine that you go to get something started?

No. Well sometimes you might just, you just, because we haven’t performed in a long time. So you know you might just do some exercises, stuff like that. You know. [plays]. Keep your fingers loose, and you know so you do things like that. And sometimes you might be just playing at the piano or something, you know, you get a creative spark and that leads to something else.
Yes, isn’t that interesting how if you could cause a creative spark to happen on purpose we would like do it all the time.

Oh see that’s the thing about creativity. Yeah, I mean real creativity. You know you never know when it’s going to come, where. Because I used to live in New York and I used to go to Manny’s, because that was back in the day that was on 48th Street where all the music stores were. And then you’d go in the store Manny’s and you’d check out the new keyboards and you’d be checking out keyboards and all of a sudden you’d check out a keyboard and you’d do something and man there comes the sound.
